note: Cool, clear skies, Thaipusam pilgrimage peak.
things_to_do: climb 670 steps or take rope car to temple peak
why_go: January brings mild 20–26°C temperatures and clear visibility, making the 450m climb comfortable. Thaipusam draws over 7 million devotees; the temple distributes blessed honey from its unique herbal idol. Hill views reward the effort.

note: Post-Thaipusam calm, pleasant mountain weather.
why_go: Temperatures remain mild (21–27°C) and Thaipusam crowds thin out. The rope car offers a gentler alternative to the 670 steps. Morning mist over the Palani Hills creates tranquil walking conditions.

note: Warming begins; still comfortable for temple visits.
things_to_do: morning rope car ride before heat builds
why_go: Temperatures rise to 25–33°C but remain manageable at 450m elevation. Fewer crowds mean shorter temple queues and peaceful spiritual time. Local food vendors offer fresh street snacks.

note: Heat peaks; climb early morning only.
why_go: April heat (28–36°C) is intense, but early mornings remain mild. Rope car beats walking. Temple stays cool and offers free water, food, and resting areas.
why_not: Afternoon temperatures exceed 35°C, making any outdoor activity uncomfortable. Dehydration risk is high.

note: Extreme heat; temple stays cooler but outdoors unbearable.
skip_reason: Peak summer heat (30–37°C) with no rainfall. Outdoor exploration impossible. Even rope car ride exposes skin to intense sun.
why_not: May is the hottest month, often exceeding 37°C by afternoon. Humidity is high and dehydration risk is critical. The 670-step climb is dangerous during peak hours.

note: Southwest monsoon begins; heavy rain and flooding risk.
skip_reason: Monsoon rains (monthly 200–400mm) make roads slippery and the 670-step climb treacherous. Flash floods on hillsides.
why_not: Monsoon transforms the Palani Hills into a challenging environment. Rain-soaked steps become dangerously slippery. Roads washing out is common.

note: Peak monsoon; temple open but travel hazardous.
skip_reason: Heavy monsoon rainfall (300–500mm monthly) continues. Landslide risk on hillside. Poor visibility.
why_not: July monsoon brings torrential rains and high landslide danger. Rope car may close without notice. Most visitors avoid this season.

note: Monsoon easing; still wet but paths clearing.
why_go: Monsoon softens by August. Rains decrease (150–250mm), and the hills become lush and green. Early morning often stays dry.
why_not: Roads remain muddy and steps slippery. Rope car closures are still possible. Landslide risk persists.

note: Monsoon retreats; humidity high but climbing safe again.
why_go: September transitions out of peak monsoon. Rainfall decreases further (80–150mm), and paths dry up. Humidity remains high (75–80%), but climbing is safe and rewarding. Lush vegetation is at its best.

note: Monsoon ends; cool and clear, ideal conditions return.
why_go: October marks the start of the best season. Northeast monsoon arrives (but is gentler in Tamil Nadu), temperatures drop to 22–30°C, and skies clear. Humidity eases. Visibility is excellent.

note: Coolest, clearest month; peak season with excellent conditions.
why_go: November offers the year's best conditions: cool (19–28°C), clear skies, low humidity. The 450m elevation makes the climb refreshing. Crowds increase but conditions warrant it.

note: Winter peak season; cool and comfortable throughout.
why_go: December is peak season. Temperatures stay cool (20–27°C) and skies remain clear. Winter crowds are manageable on weekdays. Holiday season brings festive temple atmosphere and special offerings.

note: Cool, dry; Swami spiritual season at its best.
things_to_do: learn Om recitation history at shrine
why_go: January brings ideal 20–26°C temperatures and dry conditions. The temple celebrates spiritual significance with heightened rituals. Kumbakonam's confluent waters are accessible for bathing.

note: Pleasant plains weather; fewer crowds than January.

note: Warming begins; manageable for temple stays.

note: Peak heat; only early morning temple visits feasible.

why_not: Afternoon temperatures exceed 35°C, making exposure dangerous. Dehydration is a serious concern.

note: Extreme summer heat; outdoor activities not viable.

note: Southwest monsoon; heavy rains flood plains temples.

note: Peak monsoon; travel and accommodation severely disrupted.
skip_reason: Heavy monsoon (300–500mm monthly) continues. Flooding is common. Access roads are washed out.
why_not: July monsoon brings persistent heavy rain. The Kaveri is in spate, making the region inaccessible. Flooding extends into lodges and temples.

note: Monsoon easing; rains reduce but roads still wet.
things_to_do: visit temple when dry spells allow

why_not: Roads remain muddy and unpredictable. Flooding can resume with little warning. Accommodation may still have water damage.

note: Monsoon transitions; humidity high but travel safe.
why_go: September brings lower rainfall (80–150mm) and drying conditions. Paths clear up and temples reopen fully. The region is at peak verdancy with cooler air.

note: Post-monsoon; cool, clear conditions begin.

note: Winter peak; cool and perfect for temple immersion.
